synopsis: For comparing the old and new systems, the NIST statistical handbook ties sample size to the performance difference or confidence precision that must be resolved [f5449]. It also provides exact-binomial and Wilson intervals when normal approximations fail, including small samples and probabilities near 0 or 1 [f5450]. For combination coverage and tuning, the handbook documents fractional factorial, screening, response-surface and D-optimal designs [f6804]. Response-surface designs fit local models and optimise a process after influential factors have been identified, while desirability functions combine several responses [f6967, f6968]. The supplied facts establish methodological options but give no selected sample size or application-specific design [f5449, f6804].

relations.note: Explains the purpose and sequencing of response-surface designs listed in the broader design catalogue.
Adds interval methods relevant to confidence precision when normal approximations fail.
